title: Radico Khaitan multibagger (2016–2026)
body: Price ~₹50–190 adjusted 2008–2016 (fell 74% in 2008, ₹191→₹49.6; sideways ₹76–186 for 8 years). Move began 2016–17: premiumisation (Magic Moments, later Rampur/Jaisalmer), D/E 0.77→0.15 (FY17–21), revenue +44% vs PAT +239% (₹80→271 cr) = operating leverage. FY26 PAT ~₹602 cr; premium >50% of revenue. ~38x ≈ PAT ×7.5 × P/E ×5 (18x→90x). User's '2008 UBL issue' story is wrong: UBL = United Breweries (beer). Real UB link: 1990s Mallya refused partnership → Radico built 8PM (1998). Nov 2026: ₹62k cr, 78x — priced.

data.drivers: premium mix, debt reduction, operating leverage
data.early_signals: premium volume growth while regular flat; debt-reduction guidance; raw-material cycle turn

title: NVIDIA: data-centre signal visible years before ChatGPT
body: Data-centre revenue $339M FY16 → $1.93B FY18 → $10.6B FY22 (pre-ChatGPT). Small fast segment inside a 'gaming/crypto' company. Two >50% drawdowns (2018, 2022) from gaming/crypto cycles, not the DC thesis. Post-2023 gains mostly earnings growth; forward P/E fell ~40 (mid-2025) → ~15–17x (Oct–Nov 2026). Unverified: CUDA 2006–07, AlexNet on GTX 580s, ARK early sale.

title: Eicher Motors / Royal Enfield turnaround
body: Fastest wealth creator in Motilal 2009–14 study; ~86x from ~₹32 (2005) to ~₹2,754 (split-adjusted). Pre-2020 10:1 split prices (₹27–30k) often misquoted.

title: Suzlon: same tailwind, debt destroyed it
body: Fell 99.6% from ₹430.92 (Jan 2008) to ₹1.51 (Mar 2020). Policy tailwind pattern like winners, but debt-funded expansion + share loss to foreign rivals. Lesson: debt and capital allocation separate winners from failures.

title: Amazon −94% (1999–2001)
body: Fell ~94% 1999–2001; regained peak only Oct 2009. Holding winners requires surviving huge drawdowns.

title: Indian defence PSUs 2020–25: rerating, not earnings
body: Business Standard 2023: rally mainly multiple rerating. Apr 2025 forward P/E ~2x historical (HAL 28x vs 14x; BEL 41x vs 21x). BSE PSU index ~5x Mar 2020–mid 2024 on capex ₹6→9.5 lakh cr.

title: Capital goods: 14 years to regain 2007 peak
body: Indian capital goods index took 2007→2021 to regain its peak. Warning against buying cyclicals at peak multiples.

title: Gensol Engineering fraud (2025)
body: SEBI interim order 15 Apr 2025: ₹977.75 cr loans; ₹663.89 cr for 6,400 EVs but only 4,704 bought; ₹42.94 cr allegedly to a DLF Camellias flat. Promoters resigned May 2025; order confirmed 30 Jul 2025.

title: Brightcom inflated profits
body: Deloitte forensic → SEBI found ~₹1,280 cr inflated profit FY19–20 via delayed write-downs; fines ~₹34 cr incl ₹15 cr on each promoter. Totals vary by report.

title: Vakrangee and Manpasand: auditor resignations
body: Vakrangee −84% from ₹515 after PwC resigned Apr 2018. Manpasand: Deloitte (2018) and Mehra Goel (2019) quit; MD/CFO arrested in ₹40 cr fake-invoice GST fraud. Auditor exits = red flag.

title: Kaynes Technology disclosure flag (Dec 2025)
body: Kotak Institutional flagged RPT disclosure mismatches and ₹180 cr capitalised know-how; stock −27% in six sessions; company called it a standalone disclosure error; no regulator action found.

title: Archegos and LTCM: leverage ruin
body: Archegos ~$36bn capital, ~$160bn exposure; banks lost >$10bn; Hwang 18 years. LTCM lost $4.6bn at >25:1 leverage. Same smart people; leverage forced exit.

title: Jane Street SEBI order (Bank Nifty expiry)
body: SEBI interim order 3 Jul 2025: ₹4,843.5 cr impounded; alleged net India profit ₹36,502 cr Jan 2023–Mar 2025 (options +₹43,289 cr). Alleged: buy BankNifty stocks in morning while building larger short options, sell later; marking the close. Ban lifted ~18 Jul 2025 after escrow. SAT reserved order 21 Oct 2026; no final ruling as of Nov 2026.

title: Porinju Veliyath PMS drawdown FY19–FY20
body: Equity Intelligence (own site): FY19 −31.87% vs Nifty TRI +16.45%; FY20 −51.48% vs −25.02% → ≈ −67% vs −13%. FY21 +152%. Peak investor back only ~1.03x by FY22 vs index 1.81x. Admitted 'chor stocks' backfired; LEEL Electricals loss. Fees 2% + 10% over 10% hurdle kept accruing.

title: Buffett & Munger: quality at a fair price
body: Understandable business, durable high ROIC (moat), owner-minded honest management, price below conservative intrinsic value (margin of safety), long hold. Munger: long-run return ≈ ROC (6% vs 18%). Structural edge: insurance float ~1.7x leverage at below T-bill cost; never forced to sell. Buffett's Alpha: Sharpe 0.79; alpha insignificant after BAB+QMJ.

title: Peter Lynch: categories, PEG, relentless research
body: Six categories (slow growers, stalwarts, fast growers, cyclicals, turnarounds, asset plays); PEG ~1; know the story. Real edge: 200+ company visits & ~700 annual reports/yr, ~300% turnover, up to 1,400 stocks; pre-Reg FD access. 'Buy what you know' is a starting point only.

title: Philip Fisher 15 points + scuttlebutt
body: Talk to customers, suppliers, competitors, ex-employees to verify a business. Long-term growth runway, R&D, margins, management integrity and depth.

title: Motilal Oswal QGLP / SQGLP
body: Quality (business + management), Growth, Longevity, Price (+Size). 100x study: ~47/3,500 stocks did 100x in ~12 yrs; small size at start. 8/10 fastest 2016–21 started < ₹2,000 cr mcap.

title: Marcellus Consistent Compounders + forensic filter
body: Revenue growth >10% and ROCE >15% in each of 10 years → 25–35 names → 12–15 after moat research; forensic accounting model (~10–12 ratios: CFO/EBITDA, contingent liabilities, RPTs, auditor, etc.).

title: Vijay Kedia SMILE
body: Small in size, Medium in experience, Large in aspiration, Extra-large market potential.

title: Pabrai Dhandho / cloning
body: Heads I win, tails I don't lose much. Few concentrated bets, low-risk high-uncertainty situations, openly clone great investors.

title: O'Neil CAN SLIM
body: Quarterly EPS +25% (40% preferred), annual EPS +25% over 3 yrs, ROE ≥17%, new products/highs, supply/demand, leader (RS ≥80), institutional sponsorship, market direction (follow-through day, distribution days). Stop 7–8%. No out-of-sample academic test found.

title: Minervini SEPA / Trend Template / VCP
body: 8-point trend template (price above 150/200 DMA, 200 DMA rising, 50 > 150 > 200, ≥25–30% above 52-wk low, within 25% of high, RS high). Volatility contraction pattern entries; tight stops.

title: Stan Weinstein stage analysis
body: Stage 1 base, Stage 2 advance (above rising 30-week MA) — buy only here, Stage 3 top, Stage 4 decline.

title: Qullamaggie breakouts / episodic pivots
body: Breakouts, episodic pivots (10%+ gap on news), parabolic shorts. Risk 0.25–1%/trade; win rate 25–30%; edge from large R-multiples.

title: Variant perception + pre-mortem process
body: Steinhardt: state consensus, your differing view, and the trigger that closes the gap. Klein pre-mortem: imagine failure, list reasons. Marks second-level thinking: what does the price already assume? Tiger-style bull/bear debates.

title: Position sizing and risk rules
body: Size = risk amount / stop distance. Expectancy = win% × avg win − loss% × avg loss. Fractional Kelly only (full Kelly absurd). Drawdown math: −50% needs +100%, −90% needs +900%. Illustrative portfolio: ~70% index core, satellites 3.5–4% each, max 5% at cost, total satellite ≤25%, staggered 3 tranches.

title: Warren Buffett
body: Started at 11; Graham-Newman; Partnership 1957–69 ~23.8%/yr net (no mgmt fee, 25% over 6%). Sanborn Map ~25% of assets 1958; Dempster 70% owned; AmEx 1964 salad-oil scuttlebutt. Korea picks 2004–05. 1951 return 75.8%. ~99% of wealth after 60–65. Mistakes: Berkshire textiles, Dexter Shoe, airlines 2020.

title: Peter Lynch
body: Magellan 1977–90 ~29.2%/yr (CRSP); $20M → $14B; quit at 46 ('too much time'). 'Most Magellan investors lost money' is a myth; real fact is a timing gap (dollar-weighted ~13–17%).

title: Radhakishan Damani
body: Ball bearings → broking with brother. 1992 short vs Harshad Mehta (BPL, Videocon, Sterlite). Long holds: HDFC Bank IPO, VST, Crisil, 3M, India Cements. D-Mart 2002 (EDLP ~8% below market, owned stores, pay suppliers ~10 days); slow expansion. ~90% wealth = D-Mart stake at 2017 IPO. Forbes 2026 $13.7–15.7bn. 'Bear cartel'/'week from bankruptcy' unsourced. No SEBI order found.

title: Rakesh Jhunjhunwala
body: Started 1985 with ₹5,000 + borrowed brother's clients' money. Tata Tea 1986 5,000 sh ₹43→143. Biggest wealth from 1991–92 bear trade. 'I love trading more than investing'. Titan bought 2002 at ~₹30–50 unadjusted (₹3 adjusted); 5.1% stake ₹11,087 cr ≈ 1/3 of ~₹30k cr portfolio at death. A2Z −94%. Aptech SEBI settlement 14 Jul 2021: him ~₹18.5 cr; ~₹37 cr all parties. Akasa Air co-founder.

title: Porinju Veliyath
body: Kotak floor trader 1990; Parag Parikh 1994–99; Equity Intelligence (Kochi) 2002. Value + momentum + event, 10–12 stocks/client. FY19–20 ≈ −67%. Only SEBI item: 2009 consent order (Geojit matter). 'Porinju effect' on bulk deals.

title: PR Sundar
body: Option seller (straddles/strangles). SEBI order SO/AA/EFD2/2023-24/7081 dated 25 May 2023: unregistered advisory via Telegram; fees ₹4.60 cr; repaid ₹6.08 cr; ₹46.8 lakh settlement; 1-yr bar; no admit/deny. Returns self-reported; tail losses e.g. 'lost 15 lakhs' Jan 2020.

title: Base rate: ~4% of stocks create all net wealth
body: US 1926–2016: ~58% of stocks lose to T-bills; 1,092 (4.3%) created all $35T. Global 1990–2020: ~2.4% of 63,785 firms. Implication: judge by whether a few winners pay for many losers.

title: Base rate: 87–93% of Indian individual F&O traders lose
body: FY22 89%; FY22–24 93% (>₹1.8 lakh cr); FY25 91% (net ₹1.06–1.12 lakh cr); FY26 87.7% (net ₹91,685 cr; gross ₹72,243 cr; 82.1% lose pre-costs). FY26 prop +₹44,483 cr, FPI +₹13,896 cr, 99% to algo users. <₹1 lakh portfolio = 78% of traders, 70% of losses. Decision: we don't do F&O.

title: Base rate: day traders almost all lose
body: Brazil: 97% of those persisting 300+ days lost; 0.4% earned more than a bank teller. Taiwan: <1% reliably profitable net of fees. Barber & Odean: frequent traders 11.4% vs 18.5%.

title: Twin engine: EPS growth × P/E rerating
body: Multibaggers combine earnings growth with a rising multiple (Mayer, Phelps, Motilal). Start at a low multiple so both engines can work. Radico ≈ 7.5 × 5. NVIDIA post-2023 was earnings-only (multiple fell).

title: Pattern: small fast segment hidden inside a flat company
body: NVIDIA data centre inside gaming; Uniparts construction inside farm. Read segment data, not consolidated headlines.

title: Eight early multibagger signals
body: 1 hidden fast segment; 2 mix shift → profit grows faster than revenue; 3 balance-sheet turn (debt falling); 4 policy precedes order books, map 1st/2nd/3rd-order beneficiaries; 5 distracted/distressed leader checked with dealers; 6 high utilisation + announced expansion; 7 promoter buying not pledging; 8 low starting multiple. Separators from failures: debt, governance, capital allocation.

title: Winners have brutal drawdowns
body: Amazon −94%, Apple/Microsoft/NVIDIA >80% at times, Netflix ~90% twice, NVIDIA >50% twice since 2018, Radico −74% in 2008, Berkshire halved ≥3 times (Mayer).

title: Hard disqualifiers regardless of price
body: Any promoter pledge (esp. rising); qualified audit / auditor resignation; margin step-change with no identifiable operating cause; growth funded by debt with negative CFO; promoter stake falling via preferential to obscure entities; credit-rating 'non-cooperation'; RPTs to promoter entities; SME/Telegram pump patterns.

title: Survival first: never be forced to sell
body: Buffett on LTCM: risked what they had and needed for what they didn't need. Leverage + drawdown = forced exit before compounding works. A −90% needs +900%.

title: Rich lists are founders, not stock pickers
body: Kaplan & Rauh: 69% of 2011 Forbes 400 started their own business. Damani's wealth is mainly D-Mart. Finance fortunes mostly from fund-management businesses (fees), not personal picking.

title: Behavior gap: investors earn less than their funds
body: Morningstar 2025: 8.7% vs 9.9% (1.2 pts/yr; 2.1 for volatile funds). India Axis MF 2003–22: funds 19.1% vs investors 13.8%. DALBAR noisy (848 bp 2024 vs 72 bp 2025).

title: Luck vs skill takes decades to separate
body: Mauboussin paradox of skill: as skill rises, luck matters more. Proving 2% alpha needs ~16–64 years of data. Only 3 ten-year beat-the-market streaks among 5,593 funds.

title: Savings rate and time beat chasing returns
body: ₹25k/month at 12% for 30 yrs ≈ ₹7.7 cr > ₹10k/month at 15% ≈ ₹5.6 cr. ₹1 lakh at 30% for 10 yrs ≈ ₹13.8 lakh. 20%/yr × 30 yrs = 237x vs 50%/yr × 3 yrs = 3.4x. At 6% inflation ₹1 cr in 30 yrs ≈ ₹17 lakh today.

title: AI doesn't pick winners by itself
body: Lopez-Lira & Tang: weak headline-sentiment signal (~51%); look-ahead/memorisation bias inflates LLM backtests. Alpha Arena S1 crypto: Qwen +22%, GPT-5 −62%; S1.5 stocks: 6/32 positive. AIEQ ETF ~9.7%/yr vs S&P ~14.2% over ~9 yrs. FinanceBench: retrieval-based answers often wrong. Use AI for reading, forensics, red-teaming.

title: Weaker than folklore: spin-offs, 13F cloning, magic formula
body: Spin-off edge contested after 2001; 13F 45-day lag means superstar alpha mostly earned pre-filing; magic formula works ~3 of 4 years and may have decayed. Strong evidence: value, momentum, quality (QMJ), low beta (BAB), 52-week high, post-earnings drift — gross of costs, with long drawdowns.

title: Myth: Radico rose because of a 2008 UBL issue
body: No source shows a 2008 buy-on-UB thesis. Radico fell 74% in 2008 and went sideways until 2016. UBL is United Breweries (beer).

title: Myth: Fidelity study found best investors were dead
body: No original study found. Also myth: 'most Magellan investors lost money' (Fidelity spokesman denied, 1996).

title: Myth: Jhunjhunwala bought Titan at ₹3
body: ₹3 is split/bonus-adjusted. He bought ~664,250 shares Mar–Jun 2002 at ~₹50 unadjusted (says entry ₹30 in Oct 2001).

title: Nov 2026: transformer makers showing peak margins
body: Shilchar, Voltamp, Indo Tech, Vilas: 3–4 straight quarters of falling OPM as capacity is added. Value moved to towers/T&D EPC at 14–24x with ~1.8–1.9x order cover.

title: India macro snapshot Nov 2026
body: Rupee record low ~₹96.5–97.2 (May 2026), ~₹94.2 on 13 Nov. US tariff on India 50%→18% (Feb 2026); IEEPA tariffs struck down 20 Feb 2026. India MSCI EM weight ~11–12%. FPIs sold record ₹1.66 lakh cr in 2025, ~₹2.45 lakh cr by Sep 2026; DII inflow FY26 ₹8.5 lakh cr. SIP record ₹32,490 cr Sep 2026, Oct ₹32,160 cr. RBI held 5.25% through Aug 2026. Nifty ~20.6x trailing; Smallcap 250 forward 21.9x vs 18.7x avg. STCG 20%, LTCG 12.5% over ₹1.25 lakh. STT from Apr 2026: futures 0.05%, options 0.15%.

title: We do not trade F&O or day-trade
body: Base rates (SEBI) make it negative expected value for individuals.

title: Edge before stocks
body: User called the public-screen pipeline an amateur move. No stock work without first stating our edge on the question.

title: Proposed edge: Lynch at scale
body: Claude: exhaustive reading, management promise-vs-delivery tracker, change detection, cross-domain chains, discipline. User: scuttlebutt, domain knowledge, judgment, holding. Awaiting user profile answers.
